issue.title: capacity_only scan skips only dirs with done.json, so ~74% of a real artifact tree is still parsed on every runner-slot poll
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-za.4 (verify-resource-diet) while capturing live
before/after measurements for epic sase-za (plan:202609/host_resource_diet.md).

The `capacity_only` scan mode added by sase-za.1 skips an artifact dir before parsing
any of its marker files only when `done.json` exists. Runner-slot admission
(`_RUNNER_SLOT_SCAN_OPTIONS` in `src/sase/axe/run_agent_wait_slots.py`) polls with that
mode on every parked-runner wait, so the skip rate is the whole point of the fix.

On a clean synthetic tree the mode is 8-12x cheaper than a full scan (~20-31ms vs
~250ms for 1,100 done / 100 running dirs; pinned by the perf floor
`scan_agent_artifacts.synthetic_6p_200pp.capacity_scan_facade`). On this host's real
tree it was only ~25% faster and used ~33% less RSS (~4.2s / 635MB peak vs ~5.6s /
942MB peak over 32 projects and 12,650 ace-run artifact dirs), because 9,345 of those
12,650 dirs (~74%) carry no `done.json` at all. Many of them do have
`agent_meta.stopped_at` set, i.e. the run genuinely finished; the dir just predates
reliable `done.json` writing. Every one of those dirs is parsed in full on every poll.

Two candidate remediations, either of which needs a liveness design that does not hide
a still-running agent:

1. Treat another finished signal (`agent_meta.stopped_at`, or a terminal
   `workflow_state.json` status) as done-equivalent for the `capacity_only` skip.
2. A one-time backfill/migration that writes `done.json` for historical dirs that are
   provably finished.

Related but distinct: sase-vb reports the SQLite index's active tier keeping the same
marker-less dirs alive forever and starving windowed DONE rows. Its scope is the
windowed budget math and it explicitly defers terminalizing those rows to a separate
liveness design -- which is the design this task needs.

task_type_fields.impact:
Parked runner-slot waiters on any host with real artifact history keep paying most of
the pre-epic scan cost: ~74% of dirs are still parsed in full on every poll window, so
sase-za's O(live) admission property holds on clean trees but degrades toward
O(history) exactly where the original load/swap incident was measured. The perf floor
added by sase-za.4 only guards the synthetic shape, so this gap will not fail loudly.
task_type_fields.repro:
On a host with a long artifact history, count the ace-run dirs the skip cannot fire on:

```bash
find ~/.sase/projects -type d -path '*/artifacts/ace-run/*' -mindepth 4 -maxdepth 5 \
  | while read -r d; do [ -f "$d/done.json" ] || echo "$d"; done | wc -l
```

Then time both scan modes over the same tree from this repo's venv:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -c "
from sase.core.agent_scan_facade import scan_agent_artifacts
from sase.core.agent_scan_wire import AgentArtifactScanOptionsWire
from sase.core.paths import sase_projects_dir
import time
for opts in (None, AgentArtifactScanOptionsWire(capacity_only=True)):
    t = time.monotonic()
    snap = scan_agent_artifacts(sase_projects_dir(), opts) if opts else scan_agent_artifacts(sase_projects_dir())
    print(opts is not None, round(time.monotonic() - t, 2), snap.stats.artifact_dirs_visited, len(snap.records))
"
```

Measured on athena 2026-09-10: 9,345 of 12,650 ace-run dirs have no `done.json`;
capacity-only took ~4.2s / 635MB peak RSS against ~5.6s / 942MB peak for the full scan.
